summary: Hanns-Peter Schmidt was an Indology and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg (~1953–1957) under Ludwig Alsdorf. He taught at Deccan College, Dr. Hari Singh Gour University, Tübingen, and UCLA (1965–2000).

Hans Delbrück was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Bonn (~1869–1873). He held academic posts at Frederick William University Berlin (1885) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1885–1921).

Hans Harder is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Hamburg, Heidelberg, and Halle-Wittenberg under Rahul Peter Das. He worked as an Assistent at Halle-Wittenberg (1995–2007) and joined an editorial board at Heidelberg in 2007.
Hans Hartog, an Indologist, studied at Tübingen, Kirchliche Hochschule Wuppertal/Bethel, Munich, and Marburg, earning his PhD in 1939 under Friedrich Heiler.

Hans Heinrich Schaeder was an Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies scholar. He held posts at the University of Leipzig (~1930–1931), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1931–1945), and the University of Göttingen (~1946–1957).

Hans Henrich Hock is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He completed graduate studies at Northwestern (~1964–1965) and Yale (~1965–1971) under Warren Crawford Cowgill, and became a professor of linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1967).
Hans Krahe was a linguist who held academic positions at the University of Würzburg (~1936–1946), Heidelberg University (~1947–1949), and the University of Tübingen (~1950–1965).

Hans Küng was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University, Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum (~1948–1955), and the Catholic University of Paris (~1955–1956), and held a post at Tübingen (~1960–1996).
Hans Martin Krämer is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied at Ruhr University Bochum from ~2000 to 2005 and held a post there around 2012.

Hans T. Bakker is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Jacob Ensink (~1970–1984). He held posts at Utrecht University (~1973–1989), the University of Groningen (~1989–2013), and the British Museum (retired curator, 2014).
Hans Urs von Balthasar was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Bernhard Geiger from 1924 to 1926 and attended the University of Zurich from ~1927 to 1928.
Hans Windisch was a religious studies scholar who held posts at Leiden University (1914–1929), Kiel University (~1929–1935), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1935).

Hans-Joachim Klimkeit was a scholar of religious studies, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate under Gustav Mensching (~1964–1968) and became Direktor at the University of Bonn in 1972, succeeding Mensching.
Hans-Werbin Köhler was an Indologist who studied under Eduard Hermann and completed his doctoral work under Ernst Waldschmidt.
Hansa Dhammahaso is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as director at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and the International Buddhist Studies College, both attested in 2017.
Hanung Kim is a Tibetologist and historian who earned a master's degree at Columbia University and a PhD at Harvard University under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.
Har Dayal was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Delhi (~1901–1903) and SOAS University of London (~1927–1930).

Harald Hauptmann was an archaeologist and Iranian/Central Asian scholar educated at Tübingen, Saarland, Heidelberg, and FU Berlin. His career included posts at the German Archaeological Institute, Heidelberg University (1980–1994), and DAI Istanbul (1994–2001).

Haraprasad Shastri was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Presidency University and Sanskrit College. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College (1900–1908) and later headed the Bengali and Sanskrit department at Dhaka University (1921–1924).

Hari Damodar Velankar was an Indologist who studied under Hari Mahadev Bhadkamkar. He held posts at Wilson College, Mumbai (attested 1944) and Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (Joint Director, attested 1959–1960).
